name: Ray Peat diet
lead: The Ray Peat diet is an eating pattern inspired by the writings of Raymond Peat, an American author on nutrition and physiology. Followers describe it as "pro-metabolic" and aimed at correcting hormonal imbalances and raising metabolic rate. Typical elements are milk, cheese, fruit and fruit juice, root vegetables, eggs, shellfish, muscle and organ meats, collagen, and saturated fats such as butter and coconut oil, while polyunsaturated fats are avoided.[1]

On looksmax.org the diet is discussed alongside claims about hormones, thyroid function and even height. No clinical trials of the diet were found in the sources reviewed, and the wiki records community claims as claims.
infobox: Dairy, fruit and juice, root vegetables, eggs, shellfish[1]
Polyunsaturated fats (nuts, seeds, seed oils, fatty fish)[1]

paras: As summarised in a looksmax.org post quoting a hospital dietitian, the diet emphasises healthy saturated fats, a heavy share of dairy, abundant fresh fruit and juice, root vegetables, animal protein and collagen. Followers cite the instability of PUFAs to explain why they are excluded.[1]
Community resource threads collect Peat's writings on metabolic rate and hormones, sodium and water retention, and nicotine.[2][3][4]

Forum members discuss the diet for hormones, skin and metabolism. One thread asserted that Peat gained roughly an inch in height in his 40s with DHEA supplementation; a reply expressed scepticism, noting that Peat made many other claims of rapid recovery.[5] Another thread pairs Peat's approach with raw animal-food diets.[6]
Community opinion is divided; thread titles include both enthusiastic and critical reactions.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the Ray Peat diet is treated as a metabolism and hormone optimisation approach, with competing views on its credibility.[1][5]

claims.claim: The diet raises metabolism and corrects hormonal imbalance
claims.believers: Followers say pro-metabolic foods such as dairy, fruit and low PUFA intake improve metabolic function and hormones.[1]
claims.experts: No published trials examining the diet were found in the sources reviewed.

claims.claim: Peat grew about an inch in his 40s using DHEA
claims.believers: A poster argued that Peat, as a scientist, would have measured himself accurately.[5]
claims.experts: No published study supports DHEA increasing adult height; another poster in the same thread was sceptical of the claim.[5]

card.summary: Dairy, fruit, juice and low-PUFA eating from Raymond Peat's writings; popular for hormone claims, with no trials.
card.note: Hormone and height claims come from forum anecdotes; none have been tested in published studies.

quick.overview:
The Ray Peat diet is built around milk, fruit and juice, root vegetables, eggs, shellfish and saturated fats while avoiding polyunsaturated fats. Followers say it raises metabolism and balances hormones.

No clinical trials of the diet were found. Forum discussion mixes enthusiastic reports with scepticism.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say lowering PUFA intake and eating sugar-rich, dairy-rich foods supports thyroid function and metabolic rate and lowers estrogen. These mechanisms have not been tested in published studies of the diet.
quick.risks: No harms were documented in the sources reviewed. Users in forums mention hormone-related side effects anecdotally, and extreme claims such as height gain are unsupported by published research.
